'''''Gymnogongrus griffithsiae''''' is a small uncommon [[seaweed]].

==Description==
This small [[alga]] grows to 5 cm long from a small disc. The fronds are erect, stiff and branch dichotomously in 1 plane, the tips a little flattened. In colour it is dark purplish brown. The structure is multiaxial with elongated cells surrounded cortical cells.<ref name="Bunker">{{cite book |last1=Bunker |first1=F.StP D. |last2=Brodie |first2=J.A. |last3=Maggs |first3=C.A. |last4=Bunker |first4=A.R. |year=2017 |title=Seaweeds of Britain and Ireland |edition=Second |publisher=Wild Nature Press |location=Plymouth, UK |isbn=978-0-9955673-3-7}}</ref><ref name="Dixon">{{cite book |last1=Dixon |first1=P.S. |last2=Irvine |first2=L.M. |year=1977 |title=Seaweeds of the British Isles Volume 1 Rhodophyta Part 1 Introduction, Nemaliales, Gigartinales |publisher=British Museum (Natural History) |isbn=0-565-00781-5}}</ref>

==Reproduction==
Male spermatangia are unknown.<ref name="Dixon"/><ref>{{cite book |last1=Fritsch |first1=F.E. |year=1965 |title=The Structure and Reproduction of Algae Volume 11 |publisher=Cambridge University Press}}</ref>{{fv|date=December 2024}} Carpotetasporangial outgrowths, that is sporangia containing four spores,<ref>{{cite book |last1=Irvine |first1=L.M. |year=1983 |title=Seaweeds of the British Isles Volume 1 Rhodophyta |page=99 |publisher=British Museum (Natural History) |isbn=0-565-00871-4}}</ref> by a carposporophyte outgrowth which develops during the year.<ref name="Dixon"/>

==Distribution==
Found in [[Great Britain]] and [[Ireland]] with a southern range, as far north as [[Lough Swilly]]. In the north [[Atlantic]] in the Azores in Europe to Massachusetts to Virginia in North America.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Morton |first1=O. |year=1994 |title=Marine Algae of Northern Ireland |publisher=Ulster Museum |isbn=0900761288}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Morton |first1=O. |year=2003 |title=The marine macroalgae of County Donegal, Ireland |journal=Bulletin of Irish Biogeographical Society |issue=27}}</ref>

==Habitat==
The plants grow in rock pools of the lower [[littoral]] and in the upper sublittoral.<ref name="Dixon"/>

==Possible confusion==
This species is similar to ''[[Ahnfeltia plicata]]'' which usually has wiry irregular branching.<ref name="Dixon"/>
